metadata.note: ai-explainer / claude-hai. AI Debt Tracker WEEK 5. ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00 (cold open, answered), B09 (verdict artifact), B10 (handoff) and B11 (outro) only — every body beat illustrates its concept as a native animated Remotion scene (REBUILD LAW). The four source PNGs and their SVG sources are REFERENCE in pantry/, never slotted as media. The script's five body sections become eight body beats: 0:15 splits into the graph (B01) and the ledger engine with its borrowed opening (B02); 0:50 splits into the two metrics (B03) and the new bonds the first metric is about (B04); 1:15 splits into the 66 additions (B05) and the timing bug (B06); 1:55 becomes B07; and the closing on-camera section becomes a limits beat. FIVE THINGS NOT TO GET WRONG: this is a TRADE — recall rose and precision fell, and no frame shows one without the other; the opening ledger was BORROWED from the answer key, so the tracker is not reading its own start; the diagnosis of the 26 wrong additions is Claude's judgment, not a person's; the reader is still NOT more accurate than a single model call (91% against 96%); and the week's gate records DELEGATED, not cleared.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about running my A I debt tracker end to end, from a quarter's filings to a ledger of every bond the company owes. This is week five of the A I Debt Tracker. It finds the new bonds that doing nothing cannot find. It also adds some that are not there.

shot.visual_intent: COLD OPEN LAW: the ask is the week itself. It lands ANSWERED, and the answer carries its own bad news — the rise and the fall are on the same frame from the first beat.

show.at: on 'running my AI debt tracker end to end'
show.event: The ask types into the Claude composer.

show.at: on 'it also adds some that are not there'
show.event: The result lands ANSWERED with three output lines — the third is the cost.

props.segment: Running Full Episodes from Filings to Ledger
props.command: Run the whole thing. For each company and quarter: list the filings, triage them, read the ones about debt, merge what they say into a ledger of bonds, and then check your own result. Score it against doing nothing.
output: all 95 of 95 development quarters ran end to end — 882 filings listed, 245 kept, 53 open questions raised
on 45 quarters graded bond by bond, recall rose from 90.9% to 97.8% against carrying the last report forward — 30 of the 34 newly issued bonds caught, against 0
and precision FELL, 92.8% to 90.2%: 26 of the 66 bonds it added are not in the report, and every one of them was traced

beats.narration_text: Until now the pieces worked alone. This week they run as one graph. Code lists the quarter's filings — eight hundred and eighty-two of them. Triage keeps the two hundred and forty-five about debt. A reader runs on each of those at the same time. Then code merges what they found and checks its own work. All ninety-five development quarters finished.

shot.visual_intent: A list of steps STATES a pipeline. A graph with a visible fan-out — one branch per filing, drawn side by side — shows the one thing that is new this week: the readers run at the same time, and code closes the loop after them.

show.event: The nodes light left to right, timeline first.

show.at: on 'a reader runs on each of those at the same time'
show.event: Triage fans out into three readers at once, in the accent.
The run line lands under the graph.

beats.narration_text: The second half is plain code. It merges events that describe the same bond, retires bonds that have matured, and applies the rest to the opening ledger. Anything it cannot place becomes an open question rather than a guess — fifty-three of them. And the opening ledger is borrowed from the answer key. Reading that from the filings is next week.

shot.visual_intent: The claim that would flatter this week is that the agent produced a ledger. It produced the DIFFERENCE between two ledgers, and the first one was handed to it. Drawing the opening panel with a BORROWED chip on it puts that on the same frame as the mechanism, not in a footnote.

beats.narration_text: The baseline is doing nothing: carry last quarter's debt forward. On forty-five quarters graded bond by bond, both start from the same opening ledger, so the gap is what reading added. Recall rose from ninety point nine percent to ninety-seven point eight. And precision fell, ninety-two point eight to ninety point two. That trade is the whole week.

shot.visual_intent: Two metrics, four bars, one scale. The accent means 'the tracker' on both rows, so the second row reads as the accent bar falling short — the fall is drawn, not captioned.

show.event: The baseline bar fills in each pair first.
The tracker's recall bar grows past it, in the accent.
The tracker's precision bar stops SHORT of the baseline's.

beats.narration_text: Recall is a percentage; this is what it means. Thirty-four bonds were first issued in those quarters. Carrying the last report forward finds none of them — it cannot, because it never reads anything. The tracker found thirty. That is the one thing reading buys, and it is the reason the whole graph exists.

shot.visual_intent: SHOW-DON'T-TELL: '0 of 34' as a bar is an empty rectangle and reads as a rendering fault. As 34 countable cells beside a row where 30 are filled, the zero is visibly a row of things that were there to be found and were not.

beats.narration_text: And this is what it cost. In the quarters whose report itemises its bonds, the tracker added sixty-six. Forty are real. Ten were existing notes read from a prospectus as if new. Ten were launch notices with no coupon yet. Four were the banks' option to buy more. Two were plain misreads. Every one was checked, by Claude, not by me.

One hue across the four wrong kinds keeps the accent meaning 'this is the cost' rather than five competing colours.

beats.narration_text: The first run had a bug, and it was not a misread. The filing window runs up to the day the report is filed, weeks after the quarter ends — so bonds sold after the quarter closed were landing inside it. I fixed that on development data and re-ran. Precision went from eighty-nine point two to ninety point two. Both runs are reported.

shot.visual_intent: The bug is a span, not a value, so the frame is a span. The two bands are the same rule applied to two different end points — which is exactly what the bug was. The two precision figures sit beneath them so the fix is reported as a before AND an after.

beats.narration_text: I re-checked last week's pieces on filings nobody had read. Triage found fifteen of fifteen — it passes this time, after failing at eight of nine. The reader beat pattern matching again, ninety-one percent to seventy-four. Asking the model directly still reads more numbers, ninety-six, with fifteen instruments that aren't in the filings and no sentence behind any of them. And the answer key agreed on three of four reports.

B2 reads more numbers, and reports 15 instruments that are not in the filings — and not one of its numbers has a sentence behind it.

3 of 4 gradable, of 5 drawn — Applied Digital could not be graded (P44, P48) and TeraWulf is the one disagreement: a total tagged in a way the key does not read (P47). Only 2 of the 25 companies had never been hand-checked, so the draw had to be extended: three of the five reports are from companies checked before, in other quarters.

beats.narration_text: The limits. Ninety-five of ninety-five is on development quarters; the test split is untouched. Every quarter started from the answer key's ledger, so none of this shows what happens when the tracker reads its own opening. Repayments barely work — three of fourteen. And the gate says delegated, not cleared: I handed the week to Claude and have not reviewed any of it.

shot.visual_intent: Every episode in this series ends on its own limits. The borrowed opening ledger is accented here because it is the limit that touches every other number on the frame, and the gate record is drawn largest because 'nobody has checked any of this' outranks all of them.

beats.narration_text: So: one graph that takes a quarter's filings and returns a ledger of bonds, and it ran on all ninety-five development quarters. Against doing nothing, recall rose almost seven points and it caught thirty of the thirty-four new bonds, where doing nothing catches none. Precision fell, and all twenty-six wrong additions were traced. One timing bug, both runs reported. And nobody has reviewed any of it.

shot.visual_intent: Judgment beat. The artifact page is the point (ILLUSTRATE LAW carve-out). The third finding is the cost and the fifth is the gate — neither is last by accident, and neither is buried.

show.event: Five findings stagger in, one per spoken clause.

props.artifactTitle: Running Full Episodes from Filings to Ledger
props.artifactHeading: What week 5 built, and what it is allowed to claim
artifactLines: One LangGraph episode per company-quarter: code lists the filings, triage keeps the 245 about debt, a reader runs on each of those at the same time, and code merges, sweeps and applies the result to an opening ledger before checking itself. All 95 of 95 development quarters ran end to end.

On 45 quarters graded bond by bond, against carrying the last report forward: recall 90.9% to 97.8% (+6.9 points, paired, +4.7 to +9.4), and 30 of the 34 newly issued bonds caught where the baseline catches 0.

Precision FELL, 92.8% to 90.2%. Of the 66 bonds the tracker added, 40 are in the report and 26 are not — 10 existing notes read as new (P56), 10 launch notices with no coupon (P57), 4 bank options (P58) and 2 plain misreads.

One timing bug (P55): bonds sold after a quarter ended were being applied to it. Fixed on development data, re-run from the saved readings; precision 89.2% before the fix and 90.2% after, and both runs are reported. Recall and new bonds caught were the same in both runs.

Fresh checks on filings labelled before each run: triage 15 of 15 (it failed last week at 8 of 9), the reader 91% of fields against 74% for regex rules — and a single model call 96%, uncited. The answer key agreed on 3 of 4 gradable reports. The gate records the week DELEGATED, not CLEARED.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Before you measure the clever version, measure doing nothing — and when the clever version wins on one number and loses on another, say both out loud. Look at whether the answer reports the metric that moved the wrong way without being asked twice.

shot.visual_intent: HANDOFF LAW: a real prompt, read ALOUD and then discussed. One of exactly two typing beats. It is this week's lesson — the trade, not the headline — turned into something a viewer can run on their own work.

show.event: The prompt types into the composer.

props.command: Before you score the clever version of my pipeline, write the do-nothing baseline — the one that changes nothing and carries last time's answer forward. Run both on the same set, from the same starting point, and report EVERY metric that moved, including the ones that moved the wrong way. Then tell me in one sentence what my version buys and what it costs.
